#2066. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#2065. Manchester United to appeal Leny Yoro red card as Fernandes questions officials

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

According to Sky Sports, United intend to challenge the decision, with Isak’s chances of regaining possession central to the dispute. Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

“To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he said, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher said.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. #2062. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

#2060. Asmir Begovic reveals two things Stoke City must do to secure promotion

Stoke City have continued their incredible run of form under Mark Robins with a 2-1 home victory over Millwall on Wednesday night to send them joint top of the Championship alongside Middlesbrough.

Everything is rosy right now in the Potteries for Stoke, who can’t stop winning at the moment, with their most recent victory over Millwall extending their winning streak to five games on the spin.

The last time the Potters were on such a run was back in 2008 with Tony Pulis at the helm; they would go on to win promotion to the Premier League that year, as now with Robins in the dugout, Stoke supporters will be hoping history can repeat itself.

However, there is still a long way to go, and the club cannot afford to rest on their laurels or become complacent anytime soon, as one former fan favourite has revealed the two things they must do to secure a Premier League return this season.

Football League World takes a closer look at the best value-for-money signings in the Championship this season

Although Stoke sit in the automatic promotion places in the Championship right now, a mere ten points separates them from 12th place; as for how good things have been, it only takes a poor couple of results to go back to reality.

Former goalkeeper and fan favourite Asmir Begovic, speaking to The Sentinel, has now revealed the two things the Potters must do this year to fire their way back to the top flight.

Begovic said: "It's not easy to get out of the Championship, but it's good to see them having a positive start. Listen, there's still a long way to go. Now we're getting into the meat and bones of the season going into the Christmas period, and it's really important to try to continue being consistent.

"They've obviously made some really good signings as well, Ethan Galbraith has been absolutely outstanding, a great signing. So for some of the things that have gone wrong, you've got to give the board and Jon Walters credit for strengthening the squad.

"Now it's about keeping that consistency, maybe adding the latter piece or two in January given their resources and positioning. The fact that the play-offs have also extended has given a lot of teams a lot more hope as well."

Do you agree with Begovic's take on the matter? What do you think Stoke must do to secure promotion? Share your thoughts below!

Begovic, 39, has had an exceptional career in professional football, beginning his career with Portsmouth before spells with Macclesfield, Bournemouth, Yeovil Town, Stoke, Chelsea, Qarabağ, AC Milan, Everton, Queen’s Park Rangers, and Leicester City.

It would be with the Potters where he would play the most games in his career, making 173 appearances across all competitions in North Staffordshire, having joined the club from Portsmouth in January 2010 for around £3.25 million, and eventually being sold to Chelsea for around £8 million.

Speaking to The Sentinel, the Bosnian has been full of praise for current Stoke number one and Sweden international Viktor Johansson, saying: "I think he certainly does have Premier League potential. I think you can see now he's being very selective with his next move. I think he wants to continue to play.

"I'm sure he would have had opportunities to go in as a number two at times, but I think the fact that he wants to play and be number one for club and country shows a lot about his character and his mentality. I think he definitely has the capabilities and talent to play in the Premier League."

Johansson penned a fresh four-year deal at the bet365 Stadium over the summer, having initially joined the club from Rotherham United in the summer of 2024 for just over £1 million, and has been exceptional ever since.

Certainly, Johansson will be hoping to play Premier League football one day, and at this rate, there is no reason it can’t be with Stoke.

Robins has been in similar positions before, but to date, has not quite gotten over the line, at least not in the Championship, falling short with Coventry City and suffering a major dip in form last year with Stoke.

The 56-year-old will be well aware of the position he is in, what he has to do, and how to do it, but should still listen to the advice the former Bosnian international has laid out before him.

The January window presents Stoke with an opportunity to add one or two fresh bodies to the mix, and if they are to get over the line, those additions could be pivotal in their year, as transfer plans must be in place ahead of the coming months, whilst remaining consistent has to be the priority for now.

Manchester United spent heavily during the summer, bringing Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba to Old Trafford for a combined £148million.

Despite the summer transfers, Michael Carrick failed to keep his job and was replaced by Mauricio Pochettino.

With United struggling, Pochettino is expected to bring a few new names in the January transfer window. The manager is reportedly expected to bring in no more than two players, with a new striker understood to be his biggest priority.

With the summer investment, the club is left with less flexibility as Pochettino looks to address several weaknesses in his squad.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could have less than £50million to spend in January, leaving the Argentine with limited room to spend during the winter transfer window.

According to reports from the Daily Mail, United are working within financial restrictions and are unlikely to sanction any major spending in January. The club are also mindful of the Premier League’s financial regulations, which could make it difficult to fund major names.

Benjamin Sesko’s injury problems and Joshua Zirkzee’s disappointing form have increased the need for another centre-forward.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is among the names linked with United. Pochettino already knows the United States international from their time together with the national team, which could make him an interesting option.

Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin and former Brentford striker Ivan Toney, currently playing for Al-Ahli, have also been mentioned as targets.

A left-back is another position United want to address. The club failed to bring in proper competition for Luke Shaw during the summer, despite being linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri.

However, the budget means Pochettino may have to choose his priorities carefully rather than address every problem in one window.

United recorded revenue of £677.6million despite not playing European football last season. However, the Premier League’s Squad Cost Ratio rules restrict spending on player and head coach wages, transfer repayments and agent fees to 85 per cent of football revenue, plus net profit from player sales.

January could become a window of careful decisions for United and Pochettino but looking at their current position and form, they need far more than just 50 million. In this budget, Pochettino needs to be careful who he brings in to improve their standings.

#2058. 'It stinks of' - David Dunn takes aim at Burnley boss Fabio Celestini

Blackburn Rovers legend David Dunn is not convinced by Burnley boss Fabio Celestini and his coaching staff, after watching how they were acting on the touchline in the East Lancashire derby last Sunday.

The two rivals were forced to share the points at Turf Moor last weekend, which extended Burnley's winless league run at home to a record-equalling 23 at the time. Their defeat on Wednesday night against Birmingham City has pushed that to a record-breaking 24.

The appointment of Fabio Celestini to replace Nicky Hayen has, so far, not gone to plan, with the same issues arising under the Swissman as there were under the Belgian.

For the most part, Burnley are great at 0-0. Only Stoke City have scored first more than the Clarets have this season. But when they have the lead, they are downright terrible, with just one win from eleven (D5 L5).

The draw against Blackburn was the third straight game in which Burnley took the lead but couldn't hold on. They did it twice, but their East Lancashire rivals found an equaliser both times.

This came after they squandered a 1-0 lead at QPR and, more memorably, a 4-1 lead at Cardiff City in the final two games before the international break, and at that point, you probably feel there's nothing more you can do to get your team to win a game.

Speaking on the Red Roses Divide podcast, Blackburn legend David Dunn noticed something that Celestini's coaching staff were doing on the touchline which, to him, "stinks of desperation."

"We mentioned last week the change in manager, and I’m still looking at the assistant or whoever it was, being more bothered about shouting at the fourth official or shouting at what was or wasn’t happening — little things like a foul that could have gone either way," he said.

"They were more interested in complaining and going nuts at the fourth official than actually watching the game. I think it was the assistant. He probably didn’t watch the game; every time I saw him, he was having a go at someone else.

"I think he got caught up in the atmosphere [of the derby], but it stinks to me of a bit of..."

"Desperation?" one of his co-hosts asked.

"Yeah, just trying to get hold of anything to help them," Dunn agreed.

Do you agree with David Dunn that Fabio Celestini and his staff are becoming desperate? Let us know in the comments.

When the game is once again being wrestled out of your control, it can be difficult to get it back, and, in Dunn's eyes, the actions to try and get one small decision after another don't paint a good picture.

Instead, perhaps a calmer approach would be apt to swing the momentum back in their favour.

Celestini was brought in with the pedigree needed to get Burnley out of this mess. The former Swiss international had success at FC Basel, despite the Swiss giant being in a crisis upon his arrival.

Taking over with the club at the bottom of the Swiss Super League, he won the domestic double with them 18 months later. They safely finished away from relegation in his first half-season, and then won the league and cup the following year.

That's what Burnley need right now: someone who can transform them in an 18-month period, before their Premier League parachute payments run out and an already troubling financial situation becomes even worse.

So far, though, it's been three draws and two defeats in five games, with their winless run now stretching to eight.

Arguably more concerning is the way they were easily beaten by Birmingham on Wednesday night, though. Blues are a good side, but Burnley's record of being good to begin games before tailing off didn't even surface against them.

Those at Turf Moor will be hoping that faith isn't being depleted among the squad.

Dunn talks about desperation — these next two weeks will be ones where Celestini and co desperately need to get their first wins and finally show some fight in this early-season relegation battle.

They put their awful home form in the rearview mirror on Saturday as they travel to Millwall, a side bang out of form off the back of four straight defeats. Only seven points separate the two, and Burnley can drag a club down towards them with a much-needed three points.

Which stadiums in the Championship, League One and League Two are the least spacious on the inside? FLW investigates...

Arguably more important is the Lancashire derby the week after, though, when Preston North End make the short trip to Turf Moor on December 6. Graham Alexander's side look to have turned a page, but they're still only a point ahead of the Clarets right now.

There are no easy games in this division, as Burnley have found out, but they're two of the more winnable ones, and with Southampton, Sheffield United and Stoke the three games after that, it'd be hard to see where a win comes from if they can't bounce back in the next fortnight.

If Celestini can't get a tune out of the side by then, Burnley could be onto their third manager of the season come the new year.

#2057. Too late, FA overturns Leny Yoro’s Liverpool red card in Pochettino’s first game

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

However, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino said.

“Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

The FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

Manchester United need to keep Ayden Heaven at the club especially with the situation surrounding the future and fitness concerns of various players. #2055. Hillsborough and Villa Park selected by Ian Wright as his favourite grounds

There are plenty of storied and famous grounds in English football, even with the increasing modernisation of the game and the move towards ‘new builds’.

Some grounds and stadiums stand the test of time through their reputation and weight of history, as well as the atmospheres that they can regularly and consistently produce.

In a country where its football pyramid remains unparalleled and the envy of the world, it is natural that the depth of quality in its infrastructure also sets a high bar.

Nostalgia permeates everything in football and there is very good reason for that – and it is no surprise, either, that it played a part in Ian Wright choosing his two favourite stadiums in English football.

Former England international Ian Wright started out at Greenwich Borough before turning professional at Crystal Palace and going on to become a legendary figure at Arsenal over a seven-year stint at Highbury in the 1990s.

After leaving Arsenal in 1998, he joined fellow London outfit West Ham United before stints at Nottingham Forest, Celtic and Burnley – retiring at the age of 36 in 2000.

Since then, Wright has become an iconic figure outside of the pitch and in broadcasting, with one of his most prominent roles nowadays as a part of the panel for The Overlap alongside Jamie Carragher, Gary Neville, Jill Scott and Roy Keane.

That storied career of Wright allowed him to experience the great, the good and the ugly of English football and so his opinion is extremely well-respected – and that will be quite nice for Sheffield Wednesday supporters, with Wright naming Hillsborough as one of his favourite grounds in England.

Alongside Aston Villa’s home of Villa Park in Birmingham, Wright chose The Owls’ stomping ground as one of his two favourite grounds in England, discussing his ‘love’ for both as a result of a nostalgic wistfulness about how they were prominent grounds for the FA Cup’s latter stages.

Wright, when asked about his favourite grounds on The Overlap, said: “For me, it’s Villa Park and Sheffield Wednesday. Yes, I like Sheffield Wednesday.

“The thing with Villa Park and Sheffield Wednesday, they used to be the semi-final venues, so I love those places when they’re full.”

Built between 1895 and 1897, Aston Villa has been the home of The Villans throughout its history, and it will remain their home for the foreseeable future.

Unlike second city rivals Birmingham City, who are moving to a new ground with their Sports Quarter project away from St Andrew’s, Villa have instead opted to regenerate the ground to move in line with UEFA standards for major international tournaments.

That is because Villa Park will be one of the stadiums used for UEFA EURO 2028, held across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

Having had a capacity of 43,205 since seating came in, it is currently down to around 37,000 due to the redevelopment but will head above 50,000 when the North Stand regeneration is complete.

UEFA EURO 2028 hosting duties come after previously also hosting matches at FIFA World Cup 1966 and UEFA EURO 1996, as well as the 1999 European Cup Winners’ Cup final between Real Mallorca and Lazio. The ground will host three group stage matches and a round of 16 tie at the tournament.

Unlike Aston Villa, who spent only three seasons outside of the Premier League before bouncing back in the last-2010’s, Sheffield Wednesday have not been able to return to the top-flight since their relegation in the 1998-99 campaign.

That has meant that the last 28 years has allowed Hillsborough to become an EFL fortress and a staple of the Championship and League One as The Owls yo-yo between the divisions.

Wednesday's 2-1 at Barnsley pushed the team up to third place in League One - for now - but the new manager thinks there's more to come from his team.

Like Villa Park, Hillsborough also hosted matches at UEFA EURO 1996, with Denmark playing all three of their games there against Portugal, Turkiye and Croatia.

The ground was also used at FIFA World Cup 1966, including the quarter-final between West Germany and Uruguay, and was selected by the FA as a proposed venue in their bid to host FIFA World Cup 2018 – but was overlooked ahead of UEFA EURO 2028.

Historic with international football and their hosting of FA Cup semi-finals, as well as even a League Cup final replay back in 1997 between Leicester City and Middlesbrough, Hillsborough is one of England’s most famous grounds, and it does get rocking when the Wednesday supporters are in full flow.

#2054. ‘Not Manchester United standard’, Paul Merson raises concerns over Manchester United squad

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have failed to hit the numbers expected off them after a lackluster campaign so far.

Michael Carrick was relieved off his duties after winning just 1 game in his first 10, while collecting only 8 points. Manchester United arr currently languishing in the relegation spots and Carrick’s successor, Mauricio Pochettino, has a massive task ahead.

Manchester United have been leaky in defence and haven’t gone a game without conceding a goal this season. Their attacking returns are equally disappointing with United failing to convert chances regularly.

Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

The January transfer window could be the first stop for Pochettino for some shopping but the budget given to him as per a previous report by readmanutd isn’t much to make a difference.

Paul Merson believes the club have several areas to improve rather than focusing only on their defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Arsenal midfielder made it clear that United need to bring in defensive reinforcements.

“Manchester United will have to get centre-halves in, defenders in and full-backs in,” Merson said.

However, Merson does not believe defensive recruitment alone will solve United’s problems. He also questioned the team’s ability to control games in midfield and expressed concerns about the quality of their attacking options.

“I wouldn’t say that’s just been the problem. I don’t think they’ve got legs in midfield, I don’t think they’re dominating games in midfield,” he explained.

He was also critical of United’s forward line, suggesting that the current attacking options are not consistently performing.

“I’ve never really been a massive fan of their front three. I think they’re not Manchester United standard, in my opinion.”

Merson also compared the current generation with some of the club’s former greats, including Wayne Rooney, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Roy Keane, Paul Scholes, David Beckham and Cristiano Ronaldo. He compared players’ consistency with those earlier.

“Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”

“And if they have a four the week after, it doesn’t really matter. So for me, it hasn’t just been the defence.”

United could face difficult decisions when the transfer window opens, particularly if they want to strengthen multiple areas of the squad and with the budget available to Pochettino, that doesn’t seem to be the case.

#2052. Ranking every 2026/27 EFL Championship club by average attendance

The EFL Championship provides great wide-ranging diversity when it comes to average home attendances, and that trend has not been bucked one bit so far in the 2026/27 campaign.

Indeed, the season's half-way point is already swiftly upon us and all 24 sides have played 17 matches in front of their home supporters ahead of this weekend's round of fixtures, with average attendance figures taking shape by this stage.

There are a handful of second-tier clubs who can call some of the country's largest stadiums home, whereas others play in grounds that wouldn't look out of place in League One or even League Two. Some clubs, meanwhile, have large capacities which simply never come close to being filled, providing a number of nuanced reasons to the context of attendances.

With that in mind, then, Football League World has decided to rank EVERY Championship club so far this season by measure of average home attendances from worst to best.

Kicking off proceedings is Lincoln City, who are in the second-tier for the first time since 1961 after winning last term's League One title against all odds and, unsurprisingly, have the division's lowest average attendance at just 10,501.

The Imps, in all fairness, play their football in the Championship's smallest stadium, and the 10,780-seater Sincil Bank virtually always operates at near-full capacity.

It's a similar story with Wrexham, with vital context required as to why the Red Dragons are only posting the Championship's second-lowest home attendance figures at 10,544.

Their Stok Cae Ras home is currently operating at a reduced capacity of 10,700 from around 12,600 owing to the redevelopment of the club's Kop Stand since the beginning of the previous campaign which, when completed, will allow more than 18,000 supporters into North Wales' largest ground.

Wrexham fans, then, are doing rather well to ensure precious few empty seats at this moment in time.

Blackburn Rovers, by contrast, are housed in one of the Championship's largest grounds, yet that doesn't prevent some of the division's worst attendance figures being posted each season without fail.

Rovers supporters are disillusioned with the club's direction under the unpopular Venky's ownership group, which is the driving force behind frequent boycotts and low attendances at their 31,367-capacity Ewood Park home.

Blackburn's average attendance falls shy of the 15,000 mark in a stadium that rarely even fills out to 50% of its total capacity, with opponents able to take thousands upon thousands of fans to East Lancashire as a result.

Across the Lancashire divide, cross-county rivals Preston North End are hardly faring much better with an average home attendance of just 16,397.

The context, of course, is that Deepdale's 23,408 capacity makes it a considerably-smaller stadium and the Lilywhites' struggles this season have clearly kept some supporters away.

QPR, meanwhile, should perhaps be doing somewhat better, although Loftus Road is among the Championship's smallest and most tightly-packed stadiums.

Despite having hosted numerous campaigns of Premier League football, the homely and traditional Loftus Road is only capable of catering to 18,360 supporters at full capacity.

Therefore, QPR's average attendance of 16,632 certainly represents a respectable figure, even if a few more seats could be taken up.

Watford's 21,557 capacity means that the Vicarage Road faithful can only ever do so much, and an average attendance of 17,636 is nothing to be sniffed at in light of the Hornets' difficulties both on and off-the-pitch.

Other clubs, mind you, provide a decent atmosphere in spite of smaller numbers that Watford simply do not offer up.

The majority of the Championship's lesser-attended clubs can be contextualised with on-pitch struggles, but that's hardly been the case with Swansea City this season.

They have enjoyed an uplifting campaign despite the departure of Vitor Matos, yet their attendance figures never vary too much and the Jack Army are averaging just shy of 18,000 supporters for each home fixture at the 21,088-capacity Swansea.com Stadium.

Charlton Athletic's 18,180 average attendance certainly poses questions considering the large capacity of the Valley, which often features more than a few vacant seats.

Indeed, it can accommodate around 27,000 supporters, but the Addicks struggle to sell-out and do see attendance figures limited by the volume of competition within the South London area.

Millwall, however, are undoubtedly making the most of their more modestly-sized 20,146-seater home less than five miles up the road, which features an average attendance of 19,305.

That figure is even greater than that of the previous campaign, in which the Lions made it all the way to the play-offs, and there's little room for attendance improvement considering that The Den can only let in just over 20,000 supporters.

Attendances throughout Lancashire have been nothing to shout about this season, yet Burnley's figures relative to stadium capacity are much more impressive.

The Clarets have also endured their fair share of challenges since returning to the Championship this term, although supporters are doing a good job of filling out the 21,994-seater Turf Moor by returning average attendances in excess of 19,000.

#2050. The untold story of Mauricio Pochettino's move to Man United: When club decided he was the right man, the moment it became 'real', emotional talks with US staff and whirlwind first days in charge

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the new head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

However, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

Patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford

As speculation raged over Carrick’s future, the odds on Pochettino replacing him at Old Trafford were slashed after some big money was placed on the 54-year-old overnight.

Preliminary talks continued with his representatives who made the US Soccer Federation aware of the situation. Pochettino discussed it over dinner at the team hotel with chief executive JT Batson and chief operating officer Dan Helfrich who knew it was pointless trying to change his mind.

‘That was the big day,’ says a source close to Pochettino, who took US team training in Fayetteville. ‘It became real and the optimism grew.’

As talks accelerated between United and their prospective new head coach, Carrick returned to Carrington to work with the United players not on international duty while chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and rubber-stamp the change.

United reached verbal agreement with Pochettino over a two-and-a-half-year deal, and agreed to pay US Soccer around £10million to buy the 54-year-old and his staff – No 2 Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino (Mauricio’s son), strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott – out of their contracts.

There was never any question of him leaving before the two Haiti ties, even though it left little time before his first game against Liverpool. Pochettino is said to have been respectful of the USA’s position and felt an obligation to see the job through.

As a compromise, it was agreed that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr would be allowed to leave for Manchester after the first leg regardless of the result.

Media in the US were informed that access to the players had been cancelled out of respect for Veterans Day. It also meant that they don’t have to answer questions about Pochettino’s future.

Carrick returned to Carrington at 7.50am for the last time as United head coach and was sacked in a meeting with Berrada and Wilcox.

By the time Pochettino woke up in Fayetteville, United officially had a managerial vacancy and he gathered the players together for a scheduled team briefing at 10am.

Pochettino went through the usual pre-match preparation, and then invited staff into the room for the second half of the meeting.

There was some emotion but no surprise when he informed them of his decision to take the United job. ‘As you’d expect, he spoke from the heart,’ says a source. ‘He loved being here but United was a dream opportunity. It was too hard to say no, but hard to say goodbye.’

United officially announced Pochettino’s appointment and confirmed that he would stay in charge for the USA’s two games against Haiti before starting work the following Wednesday.

Pochettino conducted his pre-match press conference in Fayetteville, flanked by CEO chief JT Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, and broke down in tears as he thanked them for their support over the last 26 months.

Otherwise, the preparation is said to have gone according to plan as the US squad flew to Miami.

The Argentine broke down in tears as he thanked the USA for their support over the last 26 months

The US smashed Haiti 6-0 to all but guarantee their place in the semi-finals. Even so the message from Pochettino to his players after the game was: ‘This tie isn’t over.’

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

Pochettino flew with the players from Miami to Cincinnati for the second leg at the TQL Stadium.

On a visit to the Kenwood Towne Centre shopping mall, a man whose profile had risen in the US during his two years in charge of the national team was approached by even more fans than normal.

When Pochettino appeared as a guest of honour at the NFL game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium that night, a number of Bengals’ players and staff congratulated him on his new job claiming to be United fans.

It emerged that United had provided a private jet for Pochettino and the remainder of his staff to fly straight from Cincinnati to Manchester through the night after the second leg.

In his pre-match press conference, he confirmed the departure of his three coaches over the weekend, and it was no surprise to learn that he was in constant contact over several days as he prepared to join them at Carrington.

The US beat Haiti by two goals to complete an 8-0 aggregate win. Afterwards, they played Take Me Home, Country Roads by John Denver over the stadium PA, which has been a tradition since the US hosted the World Cup last summer but carried particular poignance given that it has also been adopted as an anthem at United.

Pochettino invited all the staff onto the pitch for a team photo as he led a chant of U-S-A, and there was a tearful send-off in the dressing-room as he was presented with a signed shirt and a special hand-painted bottle of Clase Azul tequila.

It’s a favourite tipple of Pochettino’s and staff also ordered food from Chick-fil-A, which Pochettino regrets won’t be available in Manchester.

He never had a permanent residence in America, so he left the stadium at 10.30pm with the same suitcase he had brought from London and headed for Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport for the flight to Manchester.

Pochettino had a poor night’s sleep before landing shortly before noon aboard the grey Gulfstream G700 jet with D’Agostino, Scott and Tuya.

He posted a picture from the skies above Manchester and was then driven to Carrington, changing into an official United tracksuit en route.

Pochettino was too late for training but met with some of the players and club executives before being given a tour of the training ground and conducting an interview with MUTV which wrapped up about 7pm. He stayed at the training ground long into the evening to catch up on his preparation for Liverpool.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United

More players returned from international duty, but Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online. It was proof – if he needed it – that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will be under even greater scrutiny at United.

Responding, Pochettino said: 'We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

'What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

'I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about.'

Pochettino’s first training session with them at Carrington was ambushed by a drone shooting video footage that was posted online

Having only trained for a couple of hours on Thursday, Pochettino worked with the players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday.

‘The training session was a little bit longer than it normally is in (match day) minus two,’ said Pochettino at his opening pre-match press conference, admitting that he had not even had a chance to shower beforehand.

Pochettino worked with his new players between 11.30am and 2pm on Friday

Pochettino took training for the third day running at Carrington on Saturday morning, before United travelled on the team bus to their hotel where they had dinner and a pre-match meeting last night.

On Sunday he faces a massive first game as United boss in front of the cameras at Anfield at the end of a dizzying fortnight.

Manchester United are reportedly leaning towards allowing Lisandro Martinez to leave next summer, with the club increasingly doubtful about extending the defender’s contract beyond the current season.

According to GIVEMESPORT journalist Ben Jacobs, Manchester United are not expected to activate the one-year extension included in Martinez’s deal. The Argentine’s contract expires next summer, although the club retain the option to keep him until 2028.

The situation is surprising given United’s ongoing problems at the back. They have struggled to find consistency in defence, with Matthijs de Ligt still working towards full match sharpness, Leny Yoro continuing his development and Harry Maguire struggling for regular opportunities. Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs suggested that Manchester United are already considering a defensive rebuild ahead of next summer.

“I think the Lisandro Martinez direction of travel is a departure, and there is the option to extend by one year. But my gut says that Manchester United, even if they can’t get defenders in the winter, will add further in the summer,” Jacobs said.

Jacobs also suggested that activating Martinez’s extension would not necessarily mean the club intend to keep him.

“Even if Man United extend the contract, that might just be a protection so they can still sell him,” he added.

Although the decision is not yet final but Manchester United are leaning towards letting Martinez go. They find themselves in a difficult place as far as their defensive cover is concerned.
